title: Restore weighted priority scheduling across Bottleneck queue and local datastore
provenance: Transparent AI-authored injected defect family on complete pinned Bottleneck v2.19.5; not an upstream historical issue. Reference is byte-identical upstream source. Two independent mutations affect the real queue selection and weighted resource-release modules.

engineeringScope.rationale: Classified before agent runs by distinct functional modules and real scheduler/datastore integration. The integrated scenario requires both mutations to be repaired; reversing priority and fixing capacity independently each leave it failing. This is a small structural Tier2 calibration task, not evidence of measured difficulty, delegation benefit, compaction exposure or long-horizon persistence. Two small edits can repair it. publicPrompt:
Repair the shipped CommonJS local scheduler in this complete pinned Bottleneck v2.19.5 repository. This is an explicitly injected repair exercise, not a claim that upstream shipped these bugs. The active public entry point is src/lib/index.js; complete upstream documentation, CoffeeScript and bundled counterparts are available under src/.

Behavior contract: with datastore left at its local default, minTime=0, no reservoir, no expiration, and no retry handler, schedule(options, task) must preserve task results and original rejection identity. A job weight is its concurrency reservation. Running capacity is the sum of currently reserved weights, never a job count, never negative, and never above maxConcurrent. Completing a successful or failed job releases its full weight exactly once; done() accumulates the weights of completed jobs. Weight zero consumes and releases no capacity. Fully completed work leaves running() zero and all capacity reusable. A job heavier than maxConcurrent rejects without invoking its task or consuming capacity.

Jobs already running are not preempted. Among queued jobs, lower numeric priority runs first (0 highest, 9 lowest), preserving FIFO at equal priority. The highest priority queued head must fit available capacity before it starts; lower priority work does not bypass that head. Queued counts must return to zero after backlog completion. These rules must compose: after a saturated blocker releases its full capacity, a full-capacity high-priority job must precede lower-priority queued work, then its completion must allow remaining weighted work to drain in order. Repeated backlog waves must not leak reservations or jobs.

Only existing production JavaScript files under src/lib/ may change. Preserve the API and other behavior. Do not edit tests, fixtures, documentation, metadata, CoffeeScript, or bundled builds; do not add files. No installation or network is needed. Run node tests/visible.test.mjs from this actor directory. Visible tests are smoke checks; acceptance independently exercises the complete contract above. Redis, clustering, timing guarantees, retries and expiration are outside this task's tested scope.

requirements.text: Queued lower numeric priorities run first, FIFO within equal priority, without preempting running jobs.
Running concurrency is reserved weight; completion releases full weight exactly once, done totals weights, and capacity is reusable after success and failure.
Priority admission and weighted release compose across saturated backlog waves, respecting capacity and leaving no queued or reserved work.
Preserve return values and original task rejection identity; oversized jobs reject before invocation or reservation.
Zero-weight work neither reserves nor releases concurrency capacity.
